text: a The intervention effect is the regression coefficient of a linear regression analysis adjusted for baseline, age, and endocrine therapy.

b Effect sizes (ES) were calculated by dividing beta by the pooled SD at baseline, with positive ES meaning a beneficial effect of the exercise intervention on a specific outcome. ES <0.2 indicate “no effect,” ES between 0.2 and 0.5 indicate “small effects,” ES between 0.5 and 0.8 indicate “medium effects,” and ES ≥0.8 indicate “large effects.”
c Calculation for average % change between baseline and follow-up: (follow-up − baseline)/baseline × 100.
d Data of one additional patient from the control group was missing, because hippocampus size was below threshold settings.

text: TABLE 5. Exercise Intervention Effects on Cerebral Blood Flow in Breast Cancer Patients, Per Protocol Analyses
Values indicate mean (SD) and are presented in mL/100 g/minute, unless denoted otherwise.
ACC, anterior cingulate cortex; PCC, posterior cingulate cortex.
The intervention effect is the regression coefficient of a linear regression analysis adjusted for baseline, age, and endocrine therapy.
Effect sizes (ES) were calculated by dividing beta by the pooled SD at baseline, with positive ES meaning a beneficial effect of the exercise intervention on a specific outcome. ES <0.2 indicate
“no effect,” ES between 0.2 and 0.5 indicate “small effects,” ES between 0.5 and 0.8 indicate “medium effects,” and ES ≥0.8 indicate “large effects.”
Calculation for average % change between baseline and follow-up: (follow-up − baseline)/baseline × 100.
Data of one additional patient from the control group was missing, because hippocampus size was below threshold settings.
